classification_rationale: re-derived after an initial over-classification as I3 ("wrong result presented as correct") caught by check-governance-ledger.py's strict severity check: kNotConnected's repaired response is ITSELF a terminal FAILURE (the gateway's own not_connected/agent_disconnected signal), so a later genuine kApply frame overwriting it is the REAL answer superseding a placeholder -- semantically the right outcome wins, not a wrong one. The actual defect is a duplicate response_store ROW (finalize_terminal_status's NoRow-fallback inserts a second row once the first is already terminal) -- a dedup/hygiene gap (I6, capability/completeness) with the visible record still correct (I8), not I3. Predates #4672 (both call sites are unchanged in behavior by #4672, which only added applied_response=true bookkeeping to them)
summary: PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by #4672 -- Gate 7 Test 2: the accepted scope of #4672 (terminal-failure branches) does not require fixing this. trigger: each terminal branch increments the Prometheus counter BEFORE calling process_gateway_response; response_store_->store()/finalize_terminal_status log-and-continue (no propagation) on a Postgres pool-exhaustion or query error, so under PG degradation the metric fires "resolved" while the response_store row/executions-drawer entry silently fails to update
classification_rationale: re-derived after an initial over-classification as I3 caught by check-governance-ledger.py's strict severity check. Considered whether this qualifies for the I6(a) FALSE-ASSURANCE raise ("the change advertises a... data-integrity control as in force which is not in fact enforced") and concluded it does NOT: process_gateway_response's silent-degrade-on-store-failure characteristic (confirmed via `grep -n response_store_->store server/core/src/agent_service_impl.cpp`, lines 1626/1680) is a PRE-EXISTING property of the ONE shared terminal-write path, already exercised by the legitimate-response call site that predates #4672 -- #4672 does not newly PROMISE resilience against PG-layer degradation, only that gateway-layer failures resolve instead of dropping silently. This is I6 base MEDIUM (capability newly-reachable-but-imperfect), not a new false claim
summary: Filed as #4694, which also captures UP-4 (a fleet-wide gateway outage now amplifies into a PG write burst from the previously PG-write-free exhausted-unavailable path, concentrated exactly when the incident may coincide with broader infra stress) as a candidate WS-9 chaos scenario in the same issue.
